newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mounts second Albanian evacuation mission.
newsitem.headline: Italy mounts second Albanian evacuation mission.

text.p: Italy said on Saturday it had evacuated more than 20 people from the troubled southern Albanian port of Vlore on Saturday, its second such rescue in a week.
A foreign ministry spokesman said the group of Italians and Albanians were rescued by navy helicopters and were being transferred to the southern Italian port of Brindisi.
The ministry said in a statement the operation had been carried out in conjunction with the defence ministry and with the consent of the Albanian authorities.

The spokesman said about a dozen Italians were on board accompanied by several of their Albanian relatives. A number of Albanians who had helped the Italian community in Vlore were also evacuated, but the spokesman had no precise details.
"There are more than 20 altogether," he said.
On Monday Italy evacuated 35 people from Vlore and the Foreign Ministry said very few Italians now remained in southern Albania, where armed rebels have mounted an insurrection.

The statement said Italy had also arranged for food and medicines to be sent to a hospital in Vlore run by Italian nuns who appealed for urgent supplies, saying their hospital had been looted and they had nothing to treat burns and gunshot wounds.

Western countries stepped up their efforts to resolve the rebellion and a European security mission headed by former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky was due to hold talks with Albanian President Sali Berisha later on Saturday.

Rebels who hold several southern Albanian towns have spurned Berisha's offer of an amnesty during a suspension of government efforts to crush the insurrection. They have vowed to stand their ground until Berisha steps down.

Seventy Albanians fleeing unrest crossed to Italy on Friday, including 46 who made the trip in a twin-masted fishing boat. They refused to board a vessel sent to repatriate them from the town of Otranto and have said they are seeking political asylum.
They were due to be transferred to Lecce to see whether officials would consider their cases individually.
Italy, which lies just 40 miles across the Adriatic from Albania, has stepped up security this week, fearing a fresh flood of immigrants.
Tens of thousands of Albanians made a mass exodus to Italy in rusting freighters in 1991 after 45 years of Stalinist rule crumbled in Europe's poorest country.
Thousands more have followed in illegal immigration rackets.
